source: In the S bus, in the rush hour. A chap of about 26, felt hat with a cord instead of a ribbon, neck too long, as if someone’s been having a tug-of-war with it. People getting off. The chap in question gets annoyed with one of the men standing next to him. He accuses him of jostling him every time anyone goes past. A snivelling tone which is meant to be aggressive. When he sees a vacant seat he throws himself on to it. Two hours later, I meet him in the Cour de Rome, in front of the gare Saint-Lazare. He’s with a friend who’s saying: "You ought to get an extra button put on your overcoat." He shows him where (at the lapels) and why.

gens.text: At the gate, the traveler’s suitcase rested on the conveyor belt. The queue moved slowly, each person placing items gently into bins, cautiously, under the watchful eyes of the scanners. He complied, standing still, aware of the formal protocol governing such moments. The atmosphere was tense yet orderly, signs instructing every step. Everyone followed the routine, their actions mirroring the controlled environment. Two officers managed the flow, their presence a silent reminder of the rules. They checked IDs, ensuring compliance, their demeanor polite but firm. She nodded, proceeding forward, relieved to clear the checkpoint without issue.

Bags travel, entering the machine. A young woman stands at the checkpoint, directing passengers to remove laptops and belts, her voice steady and polite. She nods, gesturing for the next in line. The traveler complies, placing shoes neatly beside the tray. Meanwhile, an officer reviews documents, his eyes scanning methodically. Two steps back, another traveler waits, hands clasped, watching intently as the process unfolds. Every movement is precise, a choreography of security and trust. He returns the passport, smiling slightly, before waving her through. They move forward, the air thick with anticipation and routine.

As the queue advanced, the scanner’s hum was constant, a backdrop to the rustle of papers and the occasional beep. An officer motioned a traveler to step aside for further inspection. Two officers worked in tandem, one handling the wanding, another overseeing the X-ray screen. The traveler stood still, hands raised, as the wand swept across their body. At the entrance, a queue forms beside the checkpoint. In this controlled space, rules dictated the rhythm, and every sign reinforced the protocol, from the bold lettering on the walls to the courteous but firm tone of the officers.
